thread:
Josie Rivera: Heads up — customers reporting p99 spike on kairos-v1 for long-context (>6k tokens) requests since onboarding at 3894420000. p95 went from ~220ms to ~1.9s on hosted-us-east-1. Repro steps below.

Alvin Chen: seeing same in prod metrics. KV cache miss rate up ~37% for sessions >8k. Possibly tokenizer split changes causing increased cache fragmentation. :eyes:

Maya Patel: can you paste a curl or example input?

Josie Rivera: here's a minimal repro (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"kairos-v1","input":"[8k tokens payload]","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

Logs:

```text
2026-03-15T17:20:12Z [runtime] request=abc123 model=kairos-v1 seq_len=8192 kv_cache_hit=false duration_ms=1880
2026-03-15T17:20:12Z [tokenizer] normalized_tokens=8194 splits=+3 boundary_shift=2
2026-03-15T17:20:12Z [kernel] selected=float16_q4 slowpath=true
```

Ravi Singh: interesting — tokenizer normalization added a Unicode normalization step in v1 that can produce extra tokens on long CJK+emoji inputs. That would increase total token count and worsen batching.

Alvin Chen: KV cache keys look different for sessions where tokenizer inserted extra BOM-like tokens — leading to prefix mismatch and cache misses.

Josie Rivera: mitigation ideas:
- Roll back tokenizer normalizer on kairos-v1 to prior behavior (v1-no-norm)
- Enable "token_merge" postprocess to collapse zero-width chars
- Increase KV cache capacity for dedicated hosts temporarily
- Add temporary routing rule: route long-context (>=6k) to kairos-v1-compact (lower-latency variant) or to fallback model kairos-v0.9

Maya Patel: Oncall/system: can we add a per-route config now? I can push a routing rule to route requests with header X-Context-Length >= 6000 to kairos-v1-compact. Small change, low-risk.

Oncall-Bot: incident created INC-2026-0112 "kairos-v1 longctx p99 spike" — severity: high. Paging eng-runtime, eng-ml. :rotating_light:

eng-runtime-bot: Noted. Assigning to @Alvin and @Ravi for initial triage.

Alvin Chen: started an A/B canary: pinned 10% traffic to kairos-v1-no-norm. Early numbers — p95 down to ~400ms on that slice. Will expand to 25% if stable.

Ravi Singh: ML team will push a tokenizer fix (strip invisible control chars) to a staging build and run tokenizer-only diffs against our long-context benchmark set.

Josie Rivera: customer-facing note drafted, sending in 15m. Also opening support ticket for affected orgs and applying temporary rate limiting on requests > 10k tokens to prevent overload.

Maya Patel: any quick mitigation we can do without model deploy? Maybe a reverse-proxy layer that trims leading whitespace/zero-width chars before tokenization.

Alvin Chen: added a proto filter at the edge for now (simple regex) — seems to cut token inflation by ~2-3%. Not perfect but helps.

Ravi Singh: plan: 1) expand no-norm canary; 2) push tokenizer patch to v1-canary; 3) monitor KV-hit and p99; 4) if stable do full rollback or deploy patch.

Josie Rivera: ETA for full rollback if needed?

Alvin Chen: can rollback within 20 minutes for hosted pools. Will coordinate with infra.

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Please drop updates here. :raised_hands:

Josie Rivera: update 30m — canary at 25% shows p95=420ms p99=620ms, KV cache hit up from 63% -> 87%. Expanding to 60% now.

Ravi Singh: tokenizer patch passed benchmarks, preparing release candidate.

Josie Rivera: last update — expanded to 100% at 2:30pm UTC. Metrics back to baseline. Closing incident when we verify 1h stability.

Alvin Chen: noted. Will keep alert monitoring on for 4 hours.

Oncall-Bot: Incident INC-2026-0112 status: resolved (2026-03-15T19:12:00Z) — root cause: tokenizer normalization increased token count leading to kvcache fragmentation and cache misses; mitigation: rolled back tokenizer normalizer and applied tokenizer patch to subsequent release.
